reference_sql:
SELECT s.store_code, MIN(o.order_ts) AS first_order_ts
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY s.store_code
alternatives: SELECT s.store_code, MIN(o.order_ts) AS first_order_ts FROM orders o RIGHT JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY s.store_code

SELECT s.store_code, MIN(o.order_ts) AS first_order_ts FROM stores s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31' GROUP BY 1

other_way.sql: SELECT s.store_code, MIN(o.order_ts) AS first_order_ts FROM orders o RIGHT JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY s.store_code
other_way.tradeoff: A RIGHT JOIN to stores keeps every store as well; whichever side is kept, the year test must stay in ON.
